events.title: Emperor Jimmu's Accession (Mythological)
events.description: According to the Nihon Shoki, Emperor Jimmu ascended to the throne in 660 BCE, establishing Japan and becoming the ancestor of the unbroken imperial line. Though historically dubious, February 11 is celebrated as Japan's National Foundation Day.

events.title: Taika Reforms
events.description: Prince Naka no Ōe (later Emperor Tenji) and Nakatomi no Kamatari launched a coup, overthrowing the Soga clan and implementing the 'Taika Reforms.' Modeling after Tang China, they established a centralized ritsuryō state, laying the foundation for ancient Japan's governmental system.

events.title: Heian-kyō Established as Capital
events.description: Emperor Kanmu moved the capital to Heian-kyō (present-day Kyoto), beginning the Heian period. Heian-kyō served as Japan's capital for a millennium until the Meiji Restoration in 1868.

events.title: Kamakura Shogunate Established
events.description: Minamoto no Yoritomo was appointed Seii Taishōgun and established the shogunate in Kamakura. This was Japan's first warrior government, beginning 680 years of shogunate rule. A dual system of Emperor and Shōgun was formed.

events.title: Edo Shogunate Established
events.description: Tokugawa Ieyasu was appointed Seii Taishōgun and established the Edo Shogunate (Tokugawa Shogunate). Edo (present-day Tokyo) became the de facto capital, beginning 265 years of Tokugawa rule.

events.title: Perry's Black Ships
events.description: US Navy Commodore Perry arrived at Uraga with four warships (Black Ships), demanding Japan open to trade. This broke Japan's 200-year isolation, forcing Japan to face Western powers.

events.title: Meiji Restoration
events.description: Emperor Meiji assumed personal rule and implemented the Meiji Restoration. Abolishing domains and establishing prefectures, eliminating the class system, implementing compulsory education, and introducing Western institutions, Japan began comprehensive modernization.

events.title: Japan's Unconditional Surrender
events.description: Emperor Shōwa issued the 'Imperial Rescript on the Termination of the War,' announcing unconditional surrender. World War II ended with Japan's defeat. August 15 became Japan's 'Memorial Day for the End of the War.'

events.title: New Constitution (Peace Constitution) Enacted
events.description: Japan promulgated a new constitution, with the Emperor becoming a symbolic head of state, guaranteeing human rights, and Article 9 stipulating permanent renunciation of war and military force. This constitution remains unchanged to this day.

events.title: Tokyo Olympics and Shinkansen
events.description: Tokyo hosted the 18th Summer Olympics, showcasing Japan's postwar recovery to the world. The Tōkaidō Shinkansen began operation, opening the era of high-speed rail. This symbolized Japan joining the ranks of advanced nations.

events.title: Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Nuclear Disaster
events.description: A magnitude 9.0 mega-earthquake struck northeastern Japan, triggering a massive tsunami that killed or left missing about 20,000 people. The Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant suffered core meltdowns, the worst nuclear disaster since Chernobyl.

events.title: Reiwa Era Begins
events.description: Emperor Akihito abdicated, Emperor Naruhito ascended, and the Reiwa era began. This was Japan's first living abdication in modern history.

events.title: Jōmon Period Begins
events.description: Japan entered the Jōmon period, known for cord-marked pottery. Jōmon people engaged in hunting, gathering, and fishing, developing a unique Jōmon culture. This was an important period in Japan's prehistoric culture.

events.title: Yayoi Period Begins
events.description: Immigrants from the continent brought rice cultivation and metalworking techniques. The Yayoi period saw Japan begin agricultural society, with social stratification and formation of small states (邑国).

events.title: Yamatai Kingdom and Queen Himiko
events.description: Chinese historical records mention Yamatai Kingdom in Japan, ruled by Queen Himiko. She used shamanic practices and sent tribute to Wei. The exact location of Yamatai remains an archaeological mystery.

events.title: Kofun Period
events.description: Large burial mounds (keyhole-shaped kofun) were built throughout Japan, showing political power consolidation. The Yamato polity gradually unified Japan, forming the imperial system.

events.title: Buddhism Transmitted to Japan
events.description: The King of Baekje presented Buddha statues and sutras to Japan, officially introducing Buddhism. Buddhism profoundly influenced Japanese culture, art, and thought, coexisting with Shinto to this day.

events.title: Prince Shōtoku Becomes Regent
events.description: Prince Shōtoku (Prince Umayado) became regent, implementing the 'Twelve Level Cap and Rank System' and 'Seventeen-Article Constitution,' introducing Chinese institutions and promoting Buddhism. He's considered a founder of Japanese culture.

events.title: Heijō-kyō Established as Capital
events.description: Empress Genmei moved the capital to Heijō-kyō (present-day Nara), beginning the Nara period. Modeled after Tang's Chang'an, Japan entered the golden age of the ritsuryō state.

events.title: Compilation of Kojiki
events.description: Ō no Yasumaro compiled the Kojiki, recording Japanese mythology and history. This is Japan's oldest book, establishing the divine legitimacy of imperial rule.

events.title: Completion of Nihon Shoki
events.description: The Nihon Shoki was compiled, Japan's earliest official history. Written in classical Chinese and influenced by Chinese historiography, it records history from the age of gods to Empress Jitō.

events.title: Kokufu Culture Flourishes
events.description: Japan stopped sending envoys to Tang, developing unique national culture. Kana script matured, aristocratic culture flourished. Murasaki Shikibu wrote The Tale of Genji, Sei Shōnagon wrote The Pillow Book, reaching peaks of Japanese literature.

events.title: The Tale of Genji Published
events.description: Murasaki Shikibu created The Tale of Genji, depicting Heian aristocratic life. This novel is acclaimed as the world's earliest full-length realistic novel, a pinnacle of Japanese literature.

events.title: Hōgen and Heiji Rebellions
events.description: Power struggles among imperial family and nobility sparked civil wars, allowing warrior class to rise. The Minamoto and Taira clans began dominating politics, ending the aristocratic era.

events.title: Taira no Kiyomori Gains Power
events.description: Taira no Kiyomori became Grand Minister, reaching the peak of Taira power. Kiyomori promoted Japan-Song trade, but Taira dominance caused resentment.

events.title: Battle of Dan-no-ura and Taira Destruction
events.description: Minamoto no Yoshitsune defeated the Taira at the Battle of Dan-no-ura, destroying the Taira clan. Minamoto no Yoritomo established warrior rule, Japan entered the age of samurai governance.

events.title: First Mongol Invasion (Bun'ei)
events.description: Kublai Khan dispatched Mongol forces to invade Japan, landing in Kyushu. But encountering a typhoon (kamikaze), the Mongol fleet was damaged and forced to retreat.

events.title: Second Mongol Invasion (Kōan)
events.description: The Yuan dynasty launched another massive invasion with 140,000 troops. Japanese warriors resisted stubbornly, another typhoon struck, nearly annihilating Yuan forces. Japanese believed this was divine wind (kamikaze) protection.

events.title: Fall of Kamakura Shogunate
events.description: Emperor Go-Daigo and general Ashikaga Takauji jointly overthrew the Kamakura Shogunate, implementing 'Kenmu Restoration,' attempting to restore direct imperial rule. But the restoration failed.

events.title: Muromachi Shogunate Established
events.description: Ashikaga Takauji was appointed Seii Taishōgun, establishing the Muromachi Shogunate. But Japan fell into Nanboku-chō division, with two emperors coexisting, civil war lasting 60 years.

events.title: Unification of Northern and Southern Courts
events.description: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu mediated unification of courts. The Muromachi Shogunate entered its golden age, Yoshimitsu built Kinkaku-ji and established tributary trade with Ming China.

events.title: Ōnin War
events.description: Shogunal succession issues sparked civil war among daimyō, reducing Kyoto to ashes. The Ōnin War marked the Muromachi Shogunate's decline, Japan entered the Warring States period.

events.title: Introduction of Firearms
events.description: Portuguese sailors drifted to Tanegashima, introducing matchlock guns to Japan. Firearms changed Japanese warfare, accelerating the Sengoku period's unification process.

events.title: Christianity Introduced
events.description: Jesuit Francis Xavier arrived in Japan, beginning missionary work. Under Sengoku daimyō protection, Christianity spread, believers reaching hundreds of thousands.

events.title: Battle of Okehazama
events.description: Oda Nobunaga defeated Imagawa Yoshimoto against overwhelming odds, beginning his rise. Using innovative tactics and decisive action, Nobunaga gradually unified central Japan.

events.title: Fall of Muromachi Shogunate
events.description: Oda Nobunaga expelled the last shōgun Ashikaga Yoshiaki, ending the Muromachi Shogunate. Nobunaga pursued 'unification by military force,' attempting to unite Japan.

events.title: Honnō-ji Incident
events.description: Oda Nobunaga was betrayed by his vassal Akechi Mitsuhide at Honnō-ji in Kyoto, committing suicide. Hashiba Hideyoshi (Toyotomi Hideyoshi) avenged Nobunaga, inheriting his mission.

events.title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi Unifies Japan
events.description: Toyotomi Hideyoshi conquered the Hōjō clan in Odawara, completing Japanese unification. Hideyoshi implemented land surveys and sword hunts, consolidating rule.

events.title: Imjin War (Korean Invasions)
events.description: Toyotomi Hideyoshi twice dispatched troops to invade Korea, attempting to conquer Ming China. Under Ming reinforcements and Korean militia resistance, Japanese forces finally withdrew. The war was costly, accelerating the Toyotomi regime's decline.

events.title: Battle of Sekigahara
events.description: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeated Ishida Mitsunari's Western Army at Sekigahara, establishing hegemony. This was Japan's largest battle, determining Japan's ruler for the next 260 years.

events.title: Siege of Osaka
events.description: Tokugawa Ieyasu destroyed the Toyotomi clan, eliminating the last threat. The Sengoku period completely ended, the Edo period began a long peace.

events.title: Sakoku Policy Begins
events.description: The shogunate prohibited Japanese from going overseas, restricted foreign trade, allowing only Dutch and Chinese limited trade at Nagasaki. Japan entered over 200 years of isolation.

events.title: Shimabara Rebellion
events.description: Kyushu peasants and Christians launched a massive uprising against oppression and religious persecution. The shogunate mobilized large forces to suppress it, the rebellion failed, Christianity was completely banned.

events.title: Genroku Era Cultural Flourishing
events.description: Mid-Edo period saw townspeople culture flourish. Matsuo Bashō created haiku, Ihara Saikaku wrote ukiyo-zōshi, Chikamatsu Monzaemon wrote puppet theater scripts. Ukiyo-e art emerged.

events.title: Treaty of Peace and Amity
events.description: The shogunate was forced to sign the Treaty of Peace and Amity with the US, opening Shimoda and Hakodate ports. Japan opened up, the sakoku era ended.

events.title: Treaty of Amity and Commerce
events.description: Under US pressure, the shogunate signed the unequal Treaty of Amity and Commerce, opening more ports, losing tariff autonomy. This sparked strong domestic opposition.

events.title: Taisei Hōkan (Return of Power)
events.description: Last shōgun Tokugawa Yoshinobu returned power to the emperor, peacefully ending the Edo Shogunate. But anti-shogunate forces were unsatisfied, demanding complete abolition.

events.title: Boshin War
events.description: New government forces clashed with shogunate remnants in the Boshin War. Government forces won, shogunate forces were completely eliminated, Meiji Restoration proceeded smoothly.

events.title: Tokyo Becomes Capital
events.description: Emperor Meiji moved the capital from Edo, renamed Tokyo. Tokyo has remained Japan's capital ever since.

events.title: Shinbashi-Yokohama Railway Opens
events.description: Japan's first railway line from Shinbashi to Yokohama opened, marking the beginning of Japan's railway era. Railway construction was crucial to Japanese modernization.

events.title: Meiji Constitution Promulgated
events.description: Japan's first constitution (Meiji Constitution) was promulgated, establishing constitutional monarchy. The Imperial Diet was established, but the emperor retained enormous power.

events.title: First Sino-Japanese War
events.description: Japan and Qing China fought over Korea, Japan won. The Treaty of Shimonoseki ceded Taiwan and Penghu to Japan, with 200 million taels indemnity. Japan joined the great powers.

events.title: Anglo-Japanese Alliance
events.description: Japan signed an alliance treaty with Britain, becoming the first Asian nation to ally equally with a Western power. This greatly elevated Japan's international status.

events.title: Russo-Japanese War
events.description: Japan and Russia fought over Manchuria and Korea. Japan won at Port Arthur, Fengtian, and Tsushima Strait, the first time an Asian nation defeated a European power, shocking the world.

events.title: Annexation of Korea
events.description: Japan forced Korea to sign the Japan-Korea Annexation Treaty, formally annexing Korea. Korea became a Japanese colony, beginning 35 years of colonial rule.

events.title: Participation in World War I
events.description: Japan joined WWI citing the Anglo-Japanese Alliance, declaring war on Germany, seizing German interests in Shandong and Pacific islands. Postwar, Japan became one of the Big Five.

events.title: Great Kantō Earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck Tokyo and Yokohama, sparking fires that killed about 100,000. Post-earthquake anti-Chinese riots saw thousands of Chinese and Koreans killed.

events.title: Mukden Incident
events.description: Japan's Kwantung Army staged the Mukden Incident, occupying Manchuria. Establishing puppet state Manchukuo in the northeast, opening full-scale invasion of China.

events.title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident and Full Invasion
events.description: Japanese forces created an incident at Marco Polo Bridge, launching full-scale invasion of China. Japanese forces occupied Beiping, Shanghai, Nanjing, committing war crimes including the Nanjing Massacre.

events.title: Nanjing Massacre
events.description: After capturing Nanjing, Japanese forces conducted six weeks of massacre, rape, and looting. About 300,000 Chinese civilians and POWs were killed, one of WWII's most brutal atrocities.

events.title: Joining Axis Powers
events.description: Japan signed the Tripartite Pact with Germany and Italy, formally joining the Axis powers.

events.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
events.description: Japan attacked the US Pearl Harbor naval base in Hawaii, crippling the US Pacific Fleet. The US declared war on Japan, the Pacific War erupted.

events.title: Early Pacific War Advantage
events.description: Japanese forces swept through Southeast Asia and the Pacific, occupying Philippines, Malaya, Singapore, Burma, Indonesia, establishing the 'Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere.'

events.title: Defeat at Midway
events.description: Japan suffered catastrophic defeat at the Battle of Midway, losing four aircraft carriers. This was the Pacific War's turning point, Japan went on the defensive.

events.title: Tokyo Air Raids
events.description: US B-29 bombers firebombed Tokyo, reducing most of the city to ashes, killing about 100,000. This was one of history's deadliest single bombings.

events.title: Hiroshima Atomic Bomb
events.description: The US dropped the first atomic bomb 'Little Boy' on Hiroshima, killing about 140,000. This was humanity's first use of nuclear weapons in war.

events.title: Nagasaki Atomic Bomb
events.description: The US dropped the second atomic bomb 'Fat Man' on Nagasaki, killing about 70,000. The same day, the Soviet Union declared war on Japan, attacking Manchuria.

events.title: Allied Occupation Period
events.description: US-led Allied forces occupied Japan, with MacArthur as Supreme Commander. Democratic reforms were implemented, zaibatsu dissolved, land reform conducted, and a peace constitution drafted.

events.title: Emperor's Declaration of Humanity
events.description: The Emperor issued a rescript denying his divinity, declaring himself human rather than divine. This symbolized Japan's transition from imperial theocracy to democracy.

events.title: Korean War Special Procurements
events.description: The Korean War broke out, with massive US military procurement in Japan, stimulating economic recovery. 'Korean War special procurements' became a key opportunity for Japan's economic takeoff.

events.title: San Francisco Peace Treaty Effective
events.description: The San Francisco Peace Treaty took effect, Japan regained sovereignty, Allied occupation ended. But US bases remained, US-Japan security treaty continued.

events.title: Joining United Nations
events.description: Japan joined the UN, returning to international society. Signed the Japan-Soviet Joint Declaration with USSR, restoring relations (but Northern Territories issue unresolved).

events.title: Revision of US-Japan Security Treaty
events.description: US and Japan revised the security treaty, sparking massive opposition protests. But the treaty was finally ratified, establishing the postwar US-Japan alliance foundation.

events.title: Osaka Expo
events.description: Osaka hosted the World Expo, attracting 64 million visitors. Japan's economic strength and technological level gained world attention.

events.title: Okinawa Reversion
events.description: The US returned administrative rights of Okinawa to Japan, but US bases remained. Okinawa reversion was an important postwar diplomatic achievement.

events.title: Oil Crisis
events.description: The first oil crisis hit Japan, economy fell into recession. But Japan successfully adjusted industrial structure, shifting to energy-saving and high-tech industries.

events.title: Bubble Economy Era
events.description: Japan's economy grew rapidly, stock and real estate prices soared. Japanese companies made massive overseas acquisitions, Japan became the world's second-largest economy, 'Japan as Number One' rhetoric prevalent.

events.title: Emperor Shōwa Dies, Heisei Era Begins
events.description: Emperor Shōwa (Hirohito) died aged 87 after reigning 62 years. Emperor Akihito ascended, the Heisei era began.

events.title: Bubble Economy Collapses
events.description: Stock and real estate bubbles burst, Japan's economy entered prolonged stagnation. The 'Lost Decade' (later extended to 'Lost Two Decades') began.

events.title: Great Hanshin Earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck Kobe, killing over 6,000. One of postwar Japan's worst earthquake disasters.

events.title: Japan-Korea World Cup
events.description: Japan and South Korea co-hosted the FIFA World Cup. This was the first World Cup in Asia and first co-hosted.

events.title: Abe Shinzō's Second Cabinet
events.description: Abe Shinzō was reelected Prime Minister, implementing 'Abenomics' to revitalize the economy. Abe served until 2020, becoming Japan's longest-serving PM.

events.title: Emperor Akihito Expresses Abdication Intent
events.description: Emperor Akihito delivered a video message expressing intent to abdicate due to advancing age and difficulty performing duties. This sparked discussion of first living abdication in 200 years.

events.title: Tokyo Olympics Postponed
events.description: Due to COVID-19 pandemic, Tokyo Olympics originally scheduled for 2020 were postponed to 2021. This was the first postponement in Olympic history.

events.title: Tokyo Olympics Held
events.description: Tokyo Olympics were held during the pandemic in 'empty stadium' format. Despite controversy, the Games were successfully completed, demonstrating Japan's organizational capability.

events.title: Assassination of Abe Shinzō
events.description: Former PM Abe Shinzō was shot and killed while campaigning in Nara, shocking Japan and the international community. This was postwar Japan's most serious political assassination.
